assets.page_title: Figure 3 continued. Distance and finite cue duration

legend: Distance-duration response on four supported ring models. A1–A4, Final activity angle after 13,000 cue-free units for selected near/far prescribed cue centres; dotted lines mark the corresponding cue-normal angles. Exact qualified basals, native kinetics and fixed physical support are held within each model. Chemical sizes are C = 40; Spring uses resting C₀ = 2 and actual basal Cb = 2.044. Tested chemical durations are 1/10/100/300/1000, Spring 0.1/1/10/100/1000. At far Holmes T = 1000, R=0.040 masks direction rather than defining a zero angle. B, Native Spring near-cue final profiles show one full-strength region retained at graded translated positions, validated against a rotated exact basal profile. C, Shortest tested passing durations for two explicitly different endpoints: final angle within 15° of the cue normal at R ≥ 0.1, and final original-core excess no more than one half. A dash means no success in the tested duration set. Near Wave-pinning passes the angle gate at 1000 while retaining more than half the original-core excess, illustrating endpoint dependence. These are finite-window observations, not a unique minimum-duration search or migration prediction. Near denotes the selected nearest eligible prescribed placement at the displayed size; it is not a cross-model matched physical distance. Open symbols mark measured failure of the separate full-field final-tail criterion; compact retained chemical T = 1000 references have no invented tail flag. Lines guide the eye between tested points, with intermediate durations unmeasured. Antipodal inputs preserve the initial reflection axis, so 0°/180° far-cue outcomes do not establish a separate binary biological mechanism. The Holmes cue-associated single peak on the first sheet is at C = 30; these duration series use C = 40.
narrative: Finite near cues can leave one full-strength activity region at a graded intermediate angular position; retained angle need not be a binary old/cue outcome.
Distance changes regional depletion, retained angle and vector magnitude differently across native models. The shortest tested successful duration depends on the explicitly chosen endpoint.
